object_description: single-storey pavilion-like building under a common roof
design_condition: Placed between the street and existing school, the staggered pavilions create pre-zones and connections to the complex, but the large footprint weakens the open-space structure and requires tree removal.

positive.statement: The staggering, twisting and fanning-out achieve surprisingly good integration into the existing school complex.
The roof unites the individual buildings into an interconnected whole.
The alternation of open and closed facade areas is direct and captivating.
The diagonal arrangement of the main rooms generates attractive spatial relationships.
The well-proportioned rooms offer a certain flexibility of use.

negative.statement: The large footprint does not meet tree-protection requirements, and trees and meadow areas must be lost.
The room program is not very convincing, with a small, separated foyer and auditorium.
Outdoor entrances create very narrow entrance situations.
The daily structures are very difficult to organize when fully staffed.
The solid construction offers flexibility mainly through multiple uses rather than actual changeability.
The non-compact single-storey structure creates a high envelope and disadvantages energy performance.
